findings.text: `int(nth)` truncates or wraps values that don't fit in int before the bounds check. For example, uint64(math.MaxUint64) becomes -1 and returns the last element instead of an out-of-bounds error. On 32-bit platforms, int64(1<<32) becomes 0 and returns the first element. Fix: check bounds in the original type N, or reject values that don't round-trip through int.

raw:
The `int(nth)` conversion can silently truncate or wrap large values. For example, a uint64 value of 2^64-1 becomes -1 and returns the last element instead of an error. A uint64 of 2^32 on a 32-bit int platform becomes 0.
